question: Eagles at Cowboys on Thanksgiving 2026: will Dallas win by 7+ points, win by 1-6 points, or fail to win?

calls.reasoning: The consensus line is Dallas -1.5 (FanDuel opened Dallas -116 / Eagles -102 on the moneyline, total 49.5; VegasInsider consensus on Nov 15 had Dallas -125 on the moneyline), which implies Dallas wins about 53-55% of the time. No Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold contract was found; the spread is a near-miss contract, so it is evidence rather than an anchor. NFL margin distributions for a home favorite of 1.5-3 points put about 29-33% on Dallas by 7+ and 24-26% on Dallas by 1-6. I leaned slightly toward Dallas because the line may be stale: Dallas beat Philadelphia 38-21 in Philadelphia in October, and the Eagles are 2-7 and 1-8 against the spread, with Hurts out and an unsettled QB (Milton reportedly started over McKee recently). I didn't lean further because Dallas's defense is poor (third-most yards allowed), they are 4-6, and they just lost 46-40 to the 49ers.

calls.reasoning: I used NFL margin distributions conditioned on the spread: a standard deviation of about 13.5 points, with clustering at margins of 3, 6 and 7. The only posted line is Dallas -1.5. It matches the May FanDuel opener exactly, so it is probably a stale lookahead line. The one sign of movement is the moneyline, which drifted from -116 to -125. Dallas closed -4.5 on the road against a McKee-led Philadelphia in Week 7 and won 38-21. Since then the Eagles have kept losing (2-7, 1-8 against the spread, an unsettled QB situation). Pure power ratings would make Dallas about -6 to -7 at home. Against that, Dallas is 4-6, has a leaky and injured defense (Bland and Booker hurt in the 46-40 loss to San Francisco), and the market may know something. I settled on an effective spread of about Dallas -4: Dallas wins about 61%, with roughly 37% on a 7+ point win.
calls.reconciliation: The runs disagree mainly on how far to trust the posted Dallas -1.5. That is partly factual: is it a live line or a stale opener? I couldn't settle it fully without web access. Three things point to stale. The line matches the May FanDuel opener exactly. SI frames Philadelphia as the division favorite. And a live -1.5 at home would rate Philadelphia better now than when Dallas closed -4.5 on the road in Week 7, which doesn't fit the Eagles' later collapse. The moneyline move from -116 to -125 shows some repricing toward Dallas, though, so the line isn't entirely dead. The rest is judgment: Dallas's poor defense and 4-6 record against Philadelphia's offensive collapse. I'd bet on an effective spread near Dallas -4, which puts me close to Run 3, between Run 1's market-anchored view and Run 2's power-rating view. No prediction market exists (none was found on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold), so the bookmaker spread is a near-miss contract and counts as evidence, not as an anchor. I'm keeping the runs' reference class.
